newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rescuers pull 15th body from Australian landslide.
newsitem.headline: Rescuers pull 15th body from Australian landslide.

text.p: Rescuers on Wednesday unearthed a 15th body from the rubble of a week-old landslide at an Australian ski village and held out scant hope of more survivors.

Three people are still missing in the wreckage of two ski lodges at Thredbo, south of Sydney, but no signs of life have been found since ski instructor Stuart Diver called in a croaking voice to rescuers from his concrete tomb over four days ago.
Diver, who survived for three freezing nights trapped deep beneath the debris, continued his rapid recovery from frostbite on Wednesday at a hospital in Canberra, north of Thredbo.
A total of 19 people were buried when the steep hillside gave way late on Wednesday night, sending one lodge crashing into another below. Diver's wife, Sally, was among them.

As night fell on the scarred mountainside on Wednesday, with rain clouds threatening overhead, rescuers burrowed deeper into crushed remains of bedrooms below the same pile of concrete slabs which imprisoned Diver.
But acoustic and camera probes have failed to find more signs of life, rescuers said on Wednesday night.
"I don't have any evidence to suggest that those (missing) people are alive," said police superintendent Charlie Sanderson.
Despite the grim odds against finding another survivor, rescuers on Wednesday hastened their search, trying to reach the missing people before the weather worsened.
Tarpaulins have been pulled across the top of the unstable slope and channels have been made from corrugated iron to carry runoff water away from the search area below.
Sanderson said he hoped rescuers could reach the three missing people by Thursday. "We are hopeful that it will be either overnight or tomorrow morning," he told reporters.
But Sanderson, exhausted and emotional, declined to say that it appeared there were no more survivors.
"I'm not going to say that because we've got families down there living with this disaster and there are still people on that site we haven't reached," Sanderson said.
"Until such time as we reach all those people there's no way that we are going to say that there are no survivors."
